answer: A physical telemetry protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to cryptographically sign live environmental feeds, such as seismic readings in basalt bedrock or wind data during a gale. To spawn an identity, an attacker must expend scarce capital deploying independent physical sensors, forcing acquisition costs to spiral. However, adversaries can use predictive simulations to synthesize correlated readings, forging proofs without operating physical hardware.
